text:
marta: FYI noticed a perf regression after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. Long-seq cold starts (seqlen ~3k) show huge HBM BW spikes and KV eviction waves on prod-dev. grabbed an nsys trace and a perfetto snapshot. link: https://perfboard/reports/280112
hao: ugh. do you have the nsys summary and a short repro command?
sam: my suspicion is the batching heuristic + selector fallback — microbatcher might be collapsing to batch=1 for these long seqs which forces a smaller, memory-heavy kernel.
perf-bot: nsys profile completed: duration=18.4s, total kernel time=12.1s, memcpy H2D=0.8s, D2H=0.02s, hbm_read_bw_peak=820.3GB/s, avg_hbm_bw=610.1GB/s
marta: paste from nsys timeline (trimmed):
```
GPU timeline:
  MatMul_small tiles (many invocations)  ->  7.9s
  kv_read_prefetch (memcpy async)        ->  2.1s
  fused_matmul_large (expected fast path)->  0.3s
  nv_decouple_kv_eviction                ->  1.0s
HBM stats:
  avg_read_bw: 610.1GB/s
  sustained_spikes: 780-820GB/s windows at warmup
  dma_stalls: high
```
marta: also saw KV eviction spikes in the same windows (evictions/sec up x5). perfetto shows repeated small kernel launches with tiny inputs.
julia: i captured the kv metrics from our runtime probe during the same run:
```
kv_cache: {
  capacity_pages: 256k,
  pages_in_use_peak: 238k,
  evictions_total: 14.3k,
  eviction_rate_peak: 18.2/s,
  avg_prefetch_hits: 0.12
}
```
hao: that matches my earlier local repro. The selector chooses small-tile matmul when sequence window crosses threshold (~2048) because it conservatively assumes memory blowup. but for our actual model shapes the small-tile kernel triggers a lot more read amplification from the KV pages.
sam: actionable: 1) force the legacy fused_large kernel for seqlen>1500 and measure; 2) disable dynamic microbatch collapse so we don't fall to batch=1 on coldstarts; 3) increase kv_prefetch_window so prefetch amortizes cost.
leo: quick test suggestion: run a controlled nsys with `--sample=stack` and set environment `RR_KERNEL_POLICY=force:fused_large` plus `KV_PREFETCH_WINDOW=16`. compare hbm bw and tail latency. also capture `nvtx` ranges around kv lookup.
marta: ran forced-policy test this morning. results quick summary:
```
baseline (after selector-change): p95 latency=210ms, avg_hbm_bw=610GB/s
forced fused_large:     p95 latency=120ms, avg_hbm_bw=320GB/s
notes: eviction rate dropped ~70%, memcpy spikes reduced, kernel launch overhead decreased
```
hao: great. can you attach the perfetto links and paste the exact repro command so I can reproduce in CI runner?
marta: repro command I used:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace_forced --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=none \
  --switch-to-processes true --env RR_KERNEL_POLICY=force:fused_large --env KV_PREFETCH_WINDOW=16 \
  -- python -m tests.run_longseq_repro --model rdev-xl --seq 3072 --batch 2 --requests 50
```
perf-bot: created perf dashboard item: https://perfboard/reports/280112/compare (attached traces + perf tables)
julia: opened an issue and linked traces: ENG-4432 — "kernel selector regression causing KV thrash on long-seq coldstart". added steps and the forced-policy patch as a temporary rollback.
leo: thanks — recommended next steps in issue: add unit test that runs long-seq microbenchmark on PRs touching selector, add invariant check to avoid falling back to small-tile kernel when kv_prefetch_win>8, and schedule a perfio run on dedicated GPUs.
hao: assigning ENG-4432 to eng-runtime, tagging @sam for batching heuristics and @marta for the rollback PR. I'll kick a CI run with your repro and post results here.
marta: thanks — I'll attach the perfetto + nsys zips to the issue and open the PR for the rollback. :thumbsup!
